title: Same prompt, same AI: what Claude Code made alone vs. what it made with my notes
author: Plastic-Gear-4258
selftext:
I'm not a programmer. I wanted to test one thing: what does the same AI make on its own, and what does it make when a human plays the game and gives it notes?

The prompt was one paragraph: beautiful, engaging, eye-catching, cool mechanics, a web game for [itch.io](http://itch.io), pick the genre yourself and don't ask me anything.

Claude Code (Godot 4.7) came back with a finished game: a little moth swinging between paper lanterns, trying to outrun the night. Graphics, music, menus, all working. And it was fine. Cute. But five minutes in, I'd seen everything.

What changed it wasn't a bigger prompt. It was notes, about seventy of them. What worked best:

\- Paint over the screenshot instead of asking for "more beautiful"

\- Write the wow as scenes, not adjectives ("more wow" just gets you more glow)

\- Play it, then be specific: what I did, what happened, what I expected

\- Make it prove the fix: it recorded a flight, measured the camera shake, rebuilt the camera and measured again (about 4x steadier)

\- Play it like a player: its own tester ran 142 checks and found 18 real bugs, but never noticed that grabbing a closer lantern stopped you dead. In a swing game, momentum is the whole fun.

\- Fix it, don't rebuild it: a 3D moth built in Blender by code and an AI-video moth both failed; going back to the original painting and only fixing how it moves worked

\- Show the rules inside the game, not just on the title screen

\- Make it remember: every lesson goes into [CLAUDE.md](http://CLAUDE.md)

The lesson: the AI did exactly what I asked. It just can't see the game the way you do, or feel when it gets boring.

The game is free and runs in your browser (desktop, and phones in landscape). Links in the first comment.

replies.author: Plastic-Gear-4258
replies.body: Fair point, thanks. I pushed hard on the wow and probably overdid the background. Was it the lanterns getting lost in it, or just too much going on overall?

replies.body:
the latter: I just couldn't focus at all anywhere on the screen

perhaps. make the background more subtle?

replies.author: Plastic-Gear-4258
